title: Creating and Maintaining a Shared Knowledge Source
summary: Building a unified knowledge base across multiple AI tools like GitHub Copilot, Copilot Notebooks, Copilot Studio, and Azure AI Foundry by centralizing content in a GitHub repository, syncing to Azure Blob Storage via GitHub Actions, and planning to connect Azure AI Search for grounding. The post documents a real-world setup process using MCPs (model context protocol) to automate infrastructure provisioning and emphasizes iterative problem-solving when tools reach limitations.
key_points: Centralize knowledge in a GitHub repo with structured folders (business-central, worldbuilding, industry-practices, teaching-framework, shared-assets) and use markdown with YAML frontmatter for semantic enrichment
Use Azure Blob Storage as an intermediate layer synced from GitHub via Actions, with a Service Principal and secure secrets for authentication
Azure AI Search remains pending setup to index the blob content and enable grounding across Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry
MCPs (Model Context Protocol tools) automate infrastructure tasks but have limitations; preflight MCP capability checking prevents wasted effort before falling back to CLI or portal
Multiple ingestion pathways exist for each tool: GitHub Copilot reads repo context directly, Copilot Notebooks require file references, and Studio and Foundry both connect through Azure services
